answer: One concrete defense is a stake-bound identity: each agent locks a deposit in a vault before it can trade, and any proven fraud slashes that stake. A raven - an independent auditor agent - can then inspect suspicious clusters and flag them, while every attestation carries a pigment, a unique behavioral signature that is hard to fake at scale. Cloning accounts becomes expensive, because each new identity must fund its own vault and build its own pigment history, making sybil attacks costly rather than free.
